scenes.say: Ever wonder why your React effects rerun when you don't expect it? Let's break down what really controls useEffect.

scenes.label: useEffect
scenes.say: useEffect runs side effects after your component renders. Think data fetching or DOM updates.
The dependency array, like this one with id, tells React when to rerun the effect.
Miss a dependency? You risk stale closures or bugs. Add too many? You get extra reruns. No array? It runs every render.

scenes.question: What if you forget a dependency?
scenes.wrong: It just runs once, no problem.
scenes.right: You may get stale values or bugs. Always include all variables used inside the effect.
scenes.say: In interviews, never say missing dependencies are fine. That leads to stale values and subtle bugs. Always include every variable you use inside the effect.
